captions.instagram:
Concept redesign of a fictional restaurant. Not a client project.

Plenty of restaurant sites open with a photo slider, then ask you to email a booking request and wait for someone to write back. By the time they reply, Friday at 7 may be gone.

So we put tonight’s hours under the name and a booking card right up top: pick a date, a time and how many, then tap Book. The menu sits one scroll down as plain text.

Does your site do this? Free review at prycedigital.com/book

captions.linkedin:
Concept redesign: a fictional restaurant’s homepage, rebuilt around booking a table.

The old version opens with a five-photo slider. Below it, a note asks guests to email their preferred date, time and party size, then wait for someone to confirm. The hours are on another page.

The new one shows tonight’s hours under the name and puts a booking card first: date, time, how many people, one button. The menu sits one scroll down as plain text.

Not a client project. If your restaurant site works like the old version, I am happy to take a look: prycedigital.com/book
